title: Batch Librarian: workload profiling, heuristic scoring, and safe config apply
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver an automated recommendation engine (internal name: Batch Librarian) that profiles request workloads, generates prioritized batching + caching configs, and safely applies changes with canary/dry-run and automated rollback. This ticket covers the core data pipeline for profiling, a heuristics scoring layer for candidate configs, an online sampler for validation, and the safe-apply/rollback mechanics integrated with the Console rollout framework. The goal is measurable unit-cost reduction on typical RLHF/chat workloads while preserving 99th-percentile latency SLOs and output quality.
background: Current heuristics are manual: SREs and runtime engineers tune batch sizes and KV cache windows per model. We see repetitive patterns across customers (short-turn chat, long-context summarization, high-QPS short prompts). There is no standardized way to safely propose and apply batching changes at scale. Past experiments reduced cost but occasionally regressed tail latency or induced KV cache thrashing. Batch Librarian aims to codify profiles and safe-apply semantics so we can scale automated optimization without regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Collect and store per-customer workload signatures (sequence length histogram, tokens/request, session affinity, KV-cache-hit-rate) into workload-profiles bucket with hourly granularity
Produce candidate batching configs (microbatch size, max batch delay ms, kv-prefix-cache-window, coalescing-policy) via heuristics engine and rank by estimated cost delta and risk score
Provide an offline simulator that runs historical traces against candidate configs and outputs p50/p95/p99 latency and estimated token-cost delta
Expose a validation mode: shadow-apply of candidate config for 24h with telemetry showing no >5% p95 increase and no quality regressions (QA prompts) before a canary roll
Implement canary rollout with automated rollback triggers (latency or error increase, cache-thrashing signals) and audit logging for applied changes
End-to-end e2e test and Console UI surface for operators to view recommendations, simulate, and approve/apply changes
implementation_steps: Data plane: extend request telemetry to capture sequence length, tokens_out, model_variant, kv-cache-hit, request_group_id. Add sampling to reduce rps overhead (1% baseline, adjustable)
Ingestion: new workload-profiles pipeline (Kafka topic workload-signatures -> Flink job -> parquet in S3 partitioned by customer/model/hour)
Offline profiler: batch job that aggregates histograms, identifies session patterns and peak windows, emits profile summaries to metastore
Heuristics engine: ruleset-based generator (initial ruleset in Python) that produces candidate configs and computes estimated CPU/GPU token/sec and cost delta
Simulator: replay historical traces through runtime simulation (latency model + KV cache model) to score candidates
Online sampler: shadow-apply mechanism at gateway layer to mirror small percentage of traffic to candidate config and collect live metrics
Safe-apply workflow: submit candidate -> dry-run simulation -> shadow validation -> canary rollout -> gradual scale -> full apply with rollback guards
Console integration: UI card listing recommendations, simulator results, risk score, change history and one-click apply with optional manual approval
safety_checks: Risk scoring: combine p99 impact (simulated), KV-cache-oscillation probability, and request-penalty to compute a single risk score
Hard limits: never recommend batch delay > 200ms for low-latency tiers, never increase microbatch size for models marked 'latency-sensitive'
Canary thresholds: abort if p95 > baseline * 1.05 or error-rate > baseline + 0.5% during canary
Rollback triggers: automated rollback on sustained (>5 min) threshold breach or immediate pause on severe spikes
Quality checks: run a prompt-suite (10 representative prompts) during shadow to look for degradation in token length, stop-conditions, or hallucination proxies
metrics_and_dashboards: Unit cost estimate: estimated cost per 1M tokens before/after (runtime cost model)
Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency by model and customer for baseline vs candidate
KV cache: prefix-hit-rate and cache-thrashing indicator (eviction-rate per minute)
Rollout view: canary traffic %, real-time metrics, and rollback events
Recommendation health: number of successful recommendations vs rollbacks, mean cost saved per recommendation
rollout_plan: MVP alpha: internal-only recommendations for non-critical models (2 weeks) — observe simulator vs shadow outcomes
Beta: selected customers opt-in with manual approval required in Console (4 weeks)
Safe-default: enable auto-recommendation generation for low-risk profiles with operator review (6 weeks)
Auto-apply experimental: limited auto-apply for very low-risk candidates with automatic rollback (12 weeks after beta on success metrics)
Full launch gated on <2% rollback rate and >=5% median unit-cost improvement on pilot customers
risks_and_mitigations: Regression to latency SLOs: mitigation — conservative canary thresholds, immediate rollback, observation window before increasing traffic
Quality regressions (model outputs): mitigation — prompt-suite QA, human-in-the-loop checks during beta
Telemetry overhead: mitigation — sampling strategy and secondary low-priority telemetry path
Incorrect cost model estimates: mitigation — calibrate cost model with live data and include uncertainty bands in ranking
Customer trust/opt-out: mitigation — Console opt-out, explicit audit logs, email notifications for applied changes to admins
testing_plan: Unit tests for heuristics rule engine and simulator determinism
Integration test: replay fixture traces through the simulator and compare with runtime sandbox measurements
Load test: apply staged canary at scale on dedicated staging fleet to validate autoscaling interaction
Chaos tests: induce KV cache eviction spikes to ensure rollback triggers fire
End-to-end: operator flow (recommendation -> simulate -> shadow -> canary -> apply) exercised in staging before prod rollout
